messages:
alex_support: Hey team — customer 'Nimbus' on dedicated pool eu-west-2-reserved-3 is seeing recurring p95/p99 latency spikes and intermittent 429s for text.generate. Started ~09:30 UTC. No config changes on their side. Posting quick logs and repro steps. :eyes:

maya_sre: :eyes: can you paste the exact 429 response body and the time window?

alex_support: 429 body: '{"error":"quota_exceeded","message":"request throttled"}' seen at 2024-06-14T09:34:11Z and 09:51:02Z. p99 jumped from 180ms -> 1.7s. Customer says it correlates with other tenants' bursts.

jon_infra: Are these on fractional MIG slices or full-slot allocs? Pool label shows mixed-3x1g. I can look at node-level counters.

alex_support: Pool uses fractional MIG config, 3 tenants per A100 node. Suspect noisy neighbor. Also seeing sudden KV-cache churn in the logs.

rita_eng: Can we get the request IDs around 09:34? Also share a curl repro if you have one.

alex_support: Request IDs: r-9a1b2c3d, r-7f6e5d4c. Repro curl (from customer):

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text.generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-nimbus' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-heavy-1.5b","input":"hello","max_tokens":256}'
```

Response alternates between 200 (slow) and 429.

maya_sre: Ok. Jon — can you run these on the node that hosted that time window: `nvidia-smi mig -l` and `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` ? Also `redwoodctl pool inspect eu-west-2-reserved-3 --since 2024-06-14T09:00`

jon_infra: Ran checks — saw one neighbor tenant with 80% sustained SM utilization in bursts at 09:32–09:36. Also observed frequent kernel preemption counts. Dump fragment from node-42: 

```
node-42: SM_util_burst=78%, memory_bw_spike=540GB/s, mig_slice_0(util)=85%, mig_slice_1(util)=12%, mig_slice_2(util)=10%
kernel_preempt=[203, 217, 190]
```

jon_infra: KV cache hit rate for rw-heavy-1.5b on that node dropped from 92%->48% during spike. That explains latency increase.

rita_eng: Interesting — looks like one tenant is saturating SMs and evicting cached KV slices. Could be small-batch busy loop. Any scheduling anomalies?

jon_infra: Scheduler logs show oscillation where the autoscaler temporarily bumped capacity at 09:33 but then scaled down immediately after. Policy: burst->scale for 2min, then check. It appears the scale-down happened before KV cache warmed, creating flap.

alex_support: So customer saw throttles while autoscaler was cycling? That matches 429s.

maya_sre: For immediate mitigation I can pin Nimbus to isolated slices on a warm node (if available) or increase their reserved share. Is customer ok with brief restart?

ted_csm: Nimbus is willing to accept brief restart if it resolves production errors. They prefer a soft fix now and then follow-up on partitioning.

rita_eng: Proposed steps: 1) Apply temporary weight increase to Nimbus in pool (10% -> 30%); 2) Move noisy tenant to separate node if we can ID them; 3) Adjust autoscaler cooldown to 5m to avoid flapping; 4) Add KV-cache prewarm hook post-scale.

jon_infra: I'll run the move if approved. I found tenant ID noisy-echo with matching burst patterns. Can migrate cordon/drain sequence: `redwoodctl node migrate --from node-42 --tenant noisy-echo --target node-57`

alex_support: Please do. Also opened a customer-facing incidence note: "We are migrating a co-tenant to reduce interference; temporary restart may occur."

deploy-bot: [deploy] migration job queued: job-8734. Estimated window 2min.

jon_infra: Migration in progress — started 09:58:20Z. Observing background copy of model artifacts.

maya_sre: After migration completed at 10:02:11Z, KV-cache hit rate for Nimbus climbed back to 89%, p99 dropped to 210ms, and no further 429s in the 10:05–10:25 window. :thumbsup:

alex_support: Customer confirmed latency returned to normal and 429s stopped. They flagged this as "blocking" in the incident form — requesting postmortem and policy change.

rita_eng: I'll file a short postmortem: root cause = co-tenant SM saturation + autoscaler cooldown too short -> scale flip -> cache coldness -> transient throttles. Action items: adjust cooldown to 5m, add cache-warm hook, and evaluate stricter slice isolation for heavy-model tenants.

ted_csm: I'll communicate timeline to Nimbus and offer a limited credit for the disruption.

maya_sre: Adding monitoring alert rule: if KV-cache-hit drops >30% and p99 > 1s in same 5m window, trigger tenant isolation workflow.

alex_support: Thanks all. Saving logs to incident 2024-06-14-NIM-8734 and will attach to postmortem.

jon_infra: One follow-up: consider limiting SM quota per tenant on fractional configs to prevent single-tenant burst taking >60% SM for >30s.

rita_eng: Agreed. Will prototype a soft cap and simulate with loadgen.

alex_support: Closing thread for now — will reopen if Nimbus sees a recurrence. :checkered_flag:
